method.description: Deterministic in-repository identity reconciliation of the two Hawaii expungement-application keys. The component-to-document bindings recorded in the track-source relationships and the source-acquisition queue were compared against the asset identities the repository actually holds, as recorded in the source-artifact registry and the repository asset audit, and against the official-source evidence already recorded in the acquisition intelligence. No network retrieval, no issuer contact and no edition mutation were performed.
method.byteVerificationNote: The digests and byte counts below are the values the source-artifact registry and the repository asset audit already carry, both of which record hashState=match and binaryPresent=true for these files. They were not re-measured in this job: private/ is untracked, so no Hawaii binary is present in this worktree, and the assignment expressly forbids downloading. They are reproduced as identity of record.
method.assignmentConstraintObserved: The stop condition confines this job to retained repository assets and deterministic identity mapping, with no download and no issuer contact. Every finding below is derived from retained data. Where a question cannot be answered inside that constraint it is recorded as unresolved rather than answered from outside it — see technicalStructure.notEstablishedWithinThisAssignment.

finding.headline: HCJDC-159 and HCJDC-159B are not two documents. Hawaii publishes one expungement application, and the repository holds its current revision at matching bytes. The defect is a duplicated identity key, not an acquisition gap.
finding.queueClaim: Eight source-acquisition rows across eight tracks carry currentEditionStatus=authority_unmanifested_source and repositoryStatus=no_repository_binary, six under acquire:HI:hcjdc-159 and two under acquire:HI:hcjdc-159b, each with the currentness question 'The issuer's current revision for this document is unconfirmed.'
finding.acquisitionRequiredRationale: Nothing needs to be obtained from the Hawaii Criminal Justice Data Center. The current official binary is already held in this repository at byte identity, and the acquisition intelligence records that the same digest was retrieved from the issuer's own publication on 2026-08-03. What is missing is an edition row, not a file.

repositoryStatusContradiction.assetAuditSays: The repository asset audit records artifactId expungement-application-rev-2026-06 with presence=present, binaryPresent=true and hashState=match, status=unmanifested_repository_asset.
repositoryStatusContradiction.resolution: The queue row is wrong on its face. The binary is present; what is absent is a retained row in the adopted edition. 'No repository binary' and 'no edition row' are different failures and the queue conflated them.
repositoryStatusContradiction.correctionOwner: the queue owner; the queue is not this job's to write

whyTheTwoKeysExist.explanation: The suffix was read as a form number. HCJDC publishes exactly two forms in total — HCJDC-073 and HCJDC 159(b) — and the '(b)' is part of the single expungement application's own identifier, not a variant of a base form numbered 159. Because the Hawaii tracks were normalized in two groups, the six non-conviction and first-offender routes acquired the key HCJDC-159 while the two deferred-acceptance routes acquired HCJDC-159B, and nothing afterwards tested whether the issuer publishes two documents.
whyTheTwoKeysExist.oneFormCoversBothRoutes: The single application covers both the non-conviction and the conviction or deferred routes; the route difference shows up in what the applicant attaches, not in which form they file.
whyTheTwoKeysExist.consequenceIfLeftUnreconciled: Two edition rows, two materialization receipts and two field maps would be created for one document, and a participant packet could present two different applications for the same filing.

That is why the disposition below is an edition amendment to add a row rather than a correction to an existing one.

scopeFinding.question: Is the expungement application statewide or court-specific?
scopeFinding.basis: HCJDC is a statewide unit of the Hawaii Department of the Attorney General. The application is filed by mail with that single office for the whole State, and the integrated legal-design memo records geography.scope=statewide on all eight affected tracks with an agency destination.

contradictedRegistryFlag.explanation: The scanner scored a document that is not a court form at all as court-specific. This is the same false positive pattern already identified and corrected for the Colorado JDF family: a scope heuristic keyed on address or caption markers, applied to a document whose destination is an executive agency.
contradictedRegistryFlag.correctionOwner: the registry owner; the registry is a forbidden path for this job
contradictedRegistryFlag.correctionRequired: Set geographicScope=statewide on both artifact rows. Recorded as a handoff, not applied.

affectedTracksAndComponents.note: The track also carries a separate custom_pleading primary filing for the court stage; only the HCJDC component is in scope here.

resolutionRequired.notPerformedRationale: Collapsing the keys rewrites data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-source-relationships.json and the source-acquisition queue, and retaining the asset amends an edition. All are outside this job's ownedPaths. This job establishes the answer and stops at the boundary.
recommendedCorrections: Collapse HCJDC-159 and HCJDC-159B to one identity for the single official document HCJDC 159(b) at REV-2026-06-03, and rebind all eight components to it.
Pin sha256 1cb4f3acc20d569820379410c3aeb67c59fe3e24866932696371f25efaad935a on each of the eight track-source relationships.
Retain the held current binary as a Hawaii packet_form authority asset in the successor edition; the adopted edition retains no Hawaii packet form at all.
Mark the held Rev. 11/15/2019 copy superseded and exclude it from binding.
Correct the two source-artifact-registry rows from geographicScope=court_specific to statewide.
Correct the eight queue rows' repositoryStatus, which reads no_repository_binary for a binary the asset audit records as present.
resolutionRequired.memoEditRationale: No Hawaii memo edit is required. The memo already records the correct issuer, the correct agency destination and statewide scope on all eight tracks, and its component bindings name the document by the same two keys the relationships use. Collapsing a duplicated source key is a source-identity correction, not a legal-design change. HI.memo.json was not opened for writing.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest accurate result. It is not identity_unresolved: the document, its issuer, its title, its role, its scope and its current revision are all established, and the current bytes are held. It is not exact_identity_confirmed_current_binary_retrievable, because retrievability was not exercised in this job and because no edition row exists to retrieve against. It is not superseded_by_current_revision at the job level — that disposition belongs to the 2019 copy alone, and is recorded there. What the eight rows actually need is one identity instead of two, and an edition row where today there is none.

redundantAcquisitionWorkRemoved.rationale: Neither key should remain an open download job. One document is published, its current revision is held at byte identity, and no issuer interaction can resolve a duplicated key held in this repository.

edition13Impact.requiresNewBytesDetail: Yes. The adopted edition retains no Hawaii packet form, so the successor edition must add one. The bytes already exist in this repository at a digest three independent records agree on; nothing needs to be acquired.
edition13Impact.requiresScopeCorrectionNote: There is no edition row carrying a wrong scope. The wrong scope is on two repository registry rows, which are not edition content.
edition13Impact.requiresLicenseDispositionNote: The acquisition intelligence records no published redistribution or commercial-use restriction. That is a negative finding on restriction, not a permission, and no licence question was assigned to this job.

implementationFamilyRelationship.effectOfThisJob: One duplicated source identity becomes one document with a confirmed current revision and held bytes, and the acquisition question closes without a download for all eight rows.
implementationFamilyRelationship.familyReadinessStatement: No Hawaii implementation family is ready and this job does not assert that any is. The document is a flat PDF with zero form fields, so an official_pdf_fill component consuming it needs a coordinate-overlay renderer and a page-geometry measurement that does not yet exist. Five of the eight tracks additionally carry a separate custom_pleading court-stage filing with no template. No Hawaii source-materialization receipt exists, no Hawaii asset is present in the materialized source root, and every relationship still records corpusState=unchecked with no pinned SHA-256.
implementationFamilyRelationship.rendererObservation: flat_pdf with zero fields is the shape the coordinate_overlay lane exists for, not the acroform_fill lane. That is an observation about the artifact; assigning a renderer is not this job's act and is not performed.

expectedDownstreamEffect: The Hawaii expungement application resolves from two open acquisition keys with an unconfirmed revision to one identified statewide document at REV-2026-06-03 whose current bytes are already held, with the superseded 2019 copy identified and quarantined. Eight components across eight tracks stop pointing at a phantom second form. Edition 1.3 gains a concrete new row to add, with the digest and byte count supplied and nothing to acquire. Two downloads and one duplicate identity are removed from the backlog. No component is rebound here, no receipt is created, no renderer is assigned, no packet becomes generatable, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.
